content: 1. Fluconazole increases the plasma levels of eluxadoline by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely when co-administering these drugs. 2. Fluconazole also increases eluxadoline levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 3. Due to incomplete data on eluxadoline metabolism, caution is recommended when co-administering with strong CYP2C19 inhibitors. 4. Fluorouracil increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 5. Fluoxetine raises eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors should be used cautiously with eluxadoline due to limited metabolic data. 7. Flurbiprofen increases eluxadoline levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Fluvoxamine increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 9. Strong CYP1A2 inhibitors should be used cautiously with eluxadoline due to limited metabolic data. 10. Fostemsavir inhibits OATP1B1/3 transporters, potentially increasing eluxadoline levels. Avoid co-administration or adjust the dose of OATP1B1/3 substrates. 11. Gemfibrozil increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 12. Eluxadoline may increase plasma levels of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir due to its interaction with OATP1B1 and BCRP transporters. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of eluxadoline. 13. Eluxadoline increases glyburide levels by reducing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Ibuprofen increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Eluxadoline increases iloprost inhaled levels by reducing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 16. Eluxadoline increases imatinib levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Indomethacin increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Eluxadoline increases irinotecan levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Isoniazid increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 20. Itraconazole increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Ketoconazole increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Eluxadoline increases lapatinib levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Eluxadoline increases leflunomide levels by reducing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 24. Eluxadoline increases lenvatinib levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Letermovir, an OATP1B1/3 inhibitor, may increase eluxadoline levels. Monitor plasma concentrations and adjust therapy as needed. 26. Letrozole increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2A6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Eluxadoline increases levofloxacin levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Levoketoconazole increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 29. Eluxadoline increases levothyroxine levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Eluxadoline increases liothyronine levels by reducing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 31. Lopinavir increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Lorcaserin increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 33. Mefenamic acid increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Eluxadoline increases methotrexate levels by reducing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Methoxsalen increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Mexiletine increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 37. Eluxadoline increases midazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Eluxadoline increases mitoxantrone levels by reducing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Modafinil increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Nicardipine increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 41. Eluxadoline increases nitrofurantoin levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Omeprazole increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 43. Paroxetine increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Eluxadoline increases pimozide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 45. Piroxicam increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Eluxadoline increases pitavastatin levels by reducing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 47. Quinidine increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Eluxadoline increases quinine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 49. Eluxadoline increases riociguat levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Ritonavir increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Eluxadoline increases rosuvastatin levels by reducing its metabolism. Reduce rosuvastatin to the lowest effective dose to minimize the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. 52. Eluxadoline increases seladelpar levels. Monitor for adverse effects when co-administered with BCRP inhibitors. 53. Eluxadoline increases selexipag levels. Monitor for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects when co-administered with BCRP inhibitors. 54. Eluxadoline increases simvastatin levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Eluxadoline increases sirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 56. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases eluxadoline levels due to velpatasvir’s inhibition of OATP1B1, OATP1B3, and OATP2B1 transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Sulfadiazine increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Sulfamethoxazole increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 59. Eluxadoline increases sulfasalazine levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Eluxadoline increases tacrolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 61. Thiotepa increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Eluxadoline increases thyroid desiccated levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Ticlopidine increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
